name: Super Bowl 04 (IV) Championship Ring - Kansas City Chiefs- January 11, 1970
description:
This replica ring follows the original yellow gold construction with a red stone face, centered by a single diamond. The top reads “WORLD CHAMPIONS”, with Chiefs branding surrounding the face. The shoulders include 23–7 score details and AFL–NFL references, with a player name panel that varies across versions. The red stone and simple diamond layout reflect early-era championship styling.

\n

Most popular and commonly sold replica versions of this Super Bowl ring feature the MVP’s name (Dawson), though other player editions are sometimes produced.
shortDescription:
League: National Football League (AFC West)
Game Stadium: Tulane Stadium (New Orleans, Louisiana)
MVP: Len Dawson #16 — Quarterback; Super Bowl MVP

\n

The Kansas City Chiefs won Super Bowl IV, defeating the Minnesota Vikings 23–7 on January 11, 1970, marking the final AFL–NFL Championship before the merger. The ring reflects the 1969 season, with Len Dawson (#16) earning MVP through efficient play. The Chiefs’ defense dominated, proving AFL teams could consistently compete. Players like Otis Taylor (#89) are also commonly featured.

\n
